questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: the academic culture and networking

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was stressful as hell. I felt like I did not receive that much help, and I have never experienced so much bureaucracy. The paper work and getting the right papers , all if this was terrible

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had something called GBO, but this was for freshmen and it did not really help. The help you received would be received from other students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: International house. This is by no doubt the best housing option. However, it is not expensive

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: My dorm provided it

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Pick IHouse even though it is the most expensive housing option. You will not regret it

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My housing was amazing, but it was not as great for a lot of other students and it was super expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you apply though UCPH, then again through UC, and then when you accepted, they will help you with the rest

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot I would say.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got approximately 5 out of the 8 clases I wanted. The seniors have first priority, so I didn’t always get my first choice

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient, it takes a lot of time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level is lower than in Denmark. It feels in general more like high school also with the constant supervision as there is attandance, assignments and several tests and they all afffect your grade. There is less space for free learning

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was like first year at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As earlier mentioned it was more like high school.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Natural resource economics
Development economics
International environmental economics 
International monetary economics

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to data science
Political science colloquium 
Topics in Economic Research
Economic History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Natural resource economics and international environment economics. Natural resource economics as it was microeconomics with time series, which gave me a new and better understanding. It was also more math intensive than the other courses which I liked. Environment economics as it gave me a better understanding of a new topic and profesor was amazing.

questions.answer: There where a lot more trips to all over the US than i expexted.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was Way more expensive than i expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you could ever dream off

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: IHouse or sport clubs

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on small trips with a few people and just enjoy those magnificent moments

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Extremely easy, no culture shock at all

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just accept you will end up hanging out with other international students and you will still love it

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Always say yes, be open and tell yourself what you want to get out of every single week

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get into IHouse. The best decision

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The community I became a part of and all the friendships from around the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Staying focused on both academics and social life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
